text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected for Dedicated cluster 'dedicated-horizon-01' (region us-west-2). Source: edge-gateway -> dedicated-proxy. Trigger: 15m rolling 5xx rate > 12%. Pager: oncall_maya

oncall_maya: On it. Paging SRE and runtime. I'm joining the call. Can someone grab customer-facing status? @customerops-lee

customerops-lee: I opened a ticket with Horizon Retail CS. They report intermittent errors since ~09:12UTC, some customers seeing request failures in checkout flows. No report of data loss.

eng-rahul: Looking at runtime metrics: queue depth for dedicated-horizon-01 CPU/GPU workers spiked, KV eviction rates increased, and tail latency jumped. Logs show repeated "ERROR gateway: upstream read timeout" and 502s from inference-proxy.

eng-rahul: Paste logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:13:21Z ERROR gateway: rpc to runtime timed out after 30s id=abc123 path=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T09:13:22Z WARN runtime: kv_cache_eviction rate=0.42 keys/s tenant=tenant-xenon
2026-03-15T09:13:23Z ERROR proxy: 502 Bad Gateway from worker-12
```

sre-joel: I'm seeing heavy tail at the dedicated ingress queues. The scheduler isn't draining because one tenant has a huge burst of long-running streams. Suspect noisy neighbor (tenant-xenon).

se-chloe: Can we confirm affected customers? Is Horizon Retail pinned to this cluster only?

customerops-lee: Horizon is pinned to dedicated-horizon-01 (contractual). They're 80% traffic for that pool. We need rapid mitigation.

eng-rahul: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Reroute non-pinned Horizon traffic (if any) to fallback region; 2) Throttle tenant-xenon at the ingress firewall; 3) Enable burst capacity (reserved spare GPU) as immediate buffer; 4) Evict the noisy tenant if throttling fails. Starting step 2 now.

oncall_maya: I'll coordinate throttling and escalation. @eng-rahul, can you apply ingress token-level throttle for tenant-xenon?

eng-rahul: Running command to apply token-level rate limit and reduce concurrent streams:
```
# rate-limit controller
redwoodctl rate-limit set --cluster dedicated-horizon-01 --tenant tenant-xenon --concurrency 8 --rps 20
```

deploybot: Deployment event: rate-limit config applied to cluster dedicated-horizon-01 by eng-rahul at 2026-03-15T09:16:05Z.

sre-joel: Seeing immediate drop in queue depth from 1200 -> 420 in metrics. 5xx rate trending down from 15% -> 7% over 2 minutes. Gateway timeouts decreasing.

customerops-lee: Update to Horizon: we've applied traffic controls and are mitigating elevated errors; no data compromise; ETA 20-30m for full recovery. They're asking for postmortem and SLA credit assessment.

eng-rahul: Enabled burst capacity pool: spun up 2 reserve GPUs and routed canary jobs. Command:
```
redwoodctl capacity add --pool burst-usw --gpus 2 --attach cluster=dedicated-horizon-01
```

eng-rahul: After burst attach, 99th latency fell ~45%, error rate now ~3.2%.

oncall_maya: Good. @sre-joel please keep an eye for any evictions or cascade to other tenants. If tenant-xenon continues after 10m, we escalate to eviction.

sre-joel: Noted. Tracking KV eviction churn and worker CPU. Current KV eviction rate dropped to 0.08 keys/s. No unexpected pod restarts.

se-chloe: For the post-incident notes: root cause likely long-lived streaming sessions from tenant-xenon combined with insufficient per-tenant concurrency caps. We'll need a follow-up to enforce better per-tenant backpressure and default per-tenant quotas on Dedicated pools.

eng-rahul: Quick SQL from observability to quantify customer impact:
```
SELECT count(*) as err_count, customer_id FROM request_logs
WHERE cluster='dedicated-horizon-01' AND timestamp > '2026-03-15T09:00:00Z' AND status >= 500
GROUP BY customer_id order by err_count desc limit 10;
```
Result: HorizonRetail=1,872 errors; tenant-xenon=34,543 errors (internal).

customerops-lee: Horizon wants exact window and affected request IDs for their incident report. I'll collect and share a dump after this thread.

oncall_maya: Status update: mitigation in place, customer impact contained to degraded UX for ~20 minutes, active throttling + burst capacity resolved majority. Handing off to daytime SRE for monitoring and postmortem: @sre-joel, take lead.

sre-joel: Taking lead. I'll open an internal incident ticket, schedule a follow-up postmortem tomorrow 10:00PT, and propose immediate action items: per-tenant concurrency limits, alert tweak to catch queue rise earlier, and automated burst attach policy.

eng-rahul: Action item for runtime team: add tenant streaming duration histogram into alerts and add automatic backpressure suggestion in Optimize.

customerops-lee: Customer-facing summary prepared and sent to Horizon: basic cause, steps we took, ETA for postmortem. They've acknowledged.

deploybot: Incident incident-5469876543 transitioned to "mitigated" by oncall_maya at 2026-03-15T09:23:30Z.

oncall_maya: Closing timeline note: Root cause = noisy long-lived streams from tenant-xenon causing queueing and KV thrash on dedicated-horizon-01 -> elevated 5xx/timeouts for pinned customer HorizonRetail. Mitigations = token throttling, burst capacity attach, monitored until recovery. Next steps documented.

sre-joel: I'll post the incident ticket link and start the blameless postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
